sample_unit: respondents completing all items of the AI literacy assessment

links.outcome: AI literacy knowledge among radiation oncology staff, including model mechanics and prediction uncertainty
links.effect: Widespread deficits in fundamental model mechanics and interpretation of prediction uncertainty; Medical Physicists scored higher than Radiation Oncologists and Radiation Therapists (p < 0.001).
links.quote: However, required competencies vary by role. While the workforce exhibited strong intuition regarding data-centric risks such as bias and data drift, widespread deficits were identified in fundamental model mechanics and interpretation of prediction uncertainty.

links.outcome: Role-specific differences in AI knowledge scores among staff
links.effect: Medical Physicists scored higher than Radiation Oncologists and Radiation Therapists (p < 0.001); required competencies vary by role.
links.quote: Significant role-specific disparities emerged: Medical Physicists demonstrated higher scores than Radiation Oncologists and Radiation Therapists (p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Validated consensus-built AI literacy knowledge assessment for the radiation oncology workforce
Targeted workshops as effective as formal degrees for building AI knowledge

screen.reason: An international survey/assessment study evaluating AI literacy and readiness among radiation oncology staff to identify baseline competencies and knowledge deficits for safe clinical oversight.
